Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightPath is preparing for an internal procurement gate and our InfoSec team surfaced a few items we need clarified before we can sign your standard DPA. High level: we need a short written commitment that customer data for our EU tenant will be processed and stored in the EU by default, and a description of the exact conditions and timing for any temporary processing or telemetry that crosses region boundaries (we call these "ephemeral telemetry hops").

Specific asks attached (BrightPath_DPA_questions.pdf) — highlights below:
- Can Redwood confirm EU-only placement for our production data and KMS storage for encryption keys? If KMS is multi-region, where are keys stored/managed?
- Under what operational scenarios would data leave the EU (eg. analytics, cache-pop, DR failover)? For each scenario: max duration, notification practice, and controls.
- Request a DPA addendum that enumerates allowable subprocessors, their regions, and a transient egress SLA (max window + audit telemetry).
- Please provide your current subprocessor roster (we asked for a CSV).

We appreciate a short written response we can present to our security committee. If helpful we can schedule a 30-min call — we are in CET.

Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Short answers up front, more detail below and we'll follow up with legal for the formal addendum draft.

- EU placement: Yes. For customer accounts configured with EU residency, production data (input/output tokens, embeddings, logs needed for request routing) is stored and served from our EU cluster by default.
- KMS: Keys for EU-resident customers are managed in an EU KMS by default. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via the customer KMS integration; when customers elect BYOK the key remains in their KMS.
- Cross-region scenarios: transient telemetry may occur for three limited use cases: 1) analytics sampling for platform health (anonymized, max 48 hours retention outside EU), 2) cache-pop replication to reduce cold-start latency in adjacent regions (ephemeral, max 6 hours), 3) disaster recovery failover (activation window documented below). Each has notification thresholds and approval gates — see details.

I've pasted a concise ops summary below and attached our current subprocessor CSV. Marissa (legal) — looping you in to start the DPA addendum draft (we have a working template). Rishi — can you confirm the analytics retention/replication windows are accurate?

Operational summary (high level):
- Analytics sampling: telemetry is sampled at an aggregate level; no PII is included. Transient export allowed for up to 48 hours for processing and then scrubbed/aggregated. Notifications: automated alert to customers after the first export plus weekly summary.
- Cache-pop replication: to support low-latency edge pulls, specific model cache shards may replicate from EU -> nearest APAC/US edge for up to 6 hours; this applies only to non-authoritative caches and does not include raw request logs.
- DR failover: in the event of a documented outage of EU primary region, we may temporarily route processing to a failover region to maintain availability. Failover triggers are automated (SLO breach + operator verification). Typical window is intended to be as brief as possible; we propose an initial contractual maximum of 72 hours with mandatory post-facto report and mitigation plan.

Elaine —

Thanks for the patience. We've prepared a draft DPA addendum (attached: draft_dpa_addendum_v1.docx) that captures the commitments Chloe outlined, and includes the subprocessor CSV. Key points:

1) Residency commitment: Redwood warrants that production customer data for accounts configured for EU residency will be stored and processed in EU facilities by default. The addendum defines the term "stored and processed" and lists the service components covered.

2) KMS handling: Redwood will use EU-resident KMS instances for EU-resident accounts. Customers may opt for BYOK; when BYOK is used, key custody remains with the customer and Redwood has no access.

3) Transient cross-region processing: we enumerate three permitted scenarios (analytics, cache-pop, DR failover) with maximum windows. For BrightPath we are able to tighten windows as follows: analytics sampling export reduced to 24 hours, cache-pop replication to 2 hours, DR failover exact maximum remains 72 hours but requires pre-approval for planned failovers and immediate notification for unplanned failovers.

4) Notification & audit: Redwood will notify customers within 24 hours of any unplanned transient egress and provide a post-incident report. Redwood will provide monthly summaries of any transient hops for the prior month.

5) Subprocessors & change control: we attach our current roster and agree to 30-day notice for non-critical subprocessor additions; for critical security vendors we will provide immediate notice and an opportunity to object within 14 days.

Next steps: please review the attached draft and we can take a short call (30 min) to finalize language. Proposed times I can offer next week: Mon 09/21 10:00-11:00 CET or Tue 09/22 14:00-15:00 CET.
